Marine animals of Galiano Island (1893–2021)A catalogue of the marine animals reported from the waters around Galiano Island, from sponges and worms to fishes and marine mammals, bringing together historical collections and published reports with the community science observations gathered by the Biodiversity Galiano project since 2016. Records distinguish historical reports that have since been confirmed, those that remain unconfirmed, and species newly reported for the island.
Data paper: Simon et al. (2022), Biodiversity Data Journal 10: e76050
Diatoms of the Salish Sea (1866–2026)A catalogue of marine diatom occurrences across the Salish Sea, consolidating records from the published literature, morphological study of samples and molecular (DNA metabarcoding) surveys. Together, these records document the region’s diatom flora and how knowledge of it has accumulated since the first reports in 1866.
Data paper: Webber et al. (2026), Biodiversity Data Journal 14: e189060

Our approach to detecting biodiversity change is documented in the Protocol for the Detection of Extirpation, which walks through our framework for inferring local extinction using a tutorial dataset from Galiano Island. The protocol is described in full in our article in Plants, People, Planet.

Flora of the Saanich PeninsulaAn analysis of the vascular plant flora of the Saanich Peninsula, drawing on historical collections and community science observations to map the status of the region’s plants, track species that have not been reported in recent decades, and recognise the contributors whose records make this work possible. Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Vegetation ReportA map-based report on the vascular plant diversity of the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Region, relating historical and community science records to biogeoclimatic zones and protected areas across the biosphere. Protocol for the Detection of ExtirpationDeveloped on Galiano Island, this protocol for detecting local extinction, or extirpation, combines historical specimens, community science observations and targeted searches. Weighing the search effort spent in each species' historical and potential habitat, the protocol tests the hypothesis that a population has been lost, in line with IUCN extinction criteria. Published in Plants, People, Planet. ❓ Projects are still in active development. Have a question or feedback? Feel free to open an issue!
